Nab2 binds to polyadenosylated RNA through a zinc finger domain and that binding to polyadenylated RNA is required for correct 3′ end processing.
the zinc finger domain of nuclear poly(A) binding protein 2 (NAB2) is required for proper control of mRNA 3′ end formation.
the zinc finger domain of Nab2 is required for proper mRNA 3′ processing.

the role of polyadenosyl RNA recognition by Nab2 in mRNA 3′ processing.
the mechanisms that regulate the length of the 3′-untranslated regions of mRNA transcripts.
how polyadenosine RNAs are recognized by Nab2, a novel zinc finger-containing protein, and the role Nab2 plays in mRNA 3′ end formation.

the polyadenosine binding domain of Nab2 is critical for proper 3′-processing of mRNAs.
Nab2 is a poly(A) RNA-binding protein with a critical role in the control of 3′- end formation.
the polyadenosine recognition function of Nab2 is required for correct poly(A) tail synthesis.

Nab2 is an essential component of the nuclear polyadenosine-binding protein machinery that regulates mRNA 3′ end formation.
the Nab2 protein is an essential poly(A)-binding protein that plays a critical role in regulating the length of the poly(A) RNA tail.
